data.name: Mathilda
data.long_meaning: The name Mathilda originated from the Germanic words 'mæth' (mighty) and 'hild' (battle). It was popularized by the 13th-century German poet Walther von der Vogelweide, who wrote a song about a female warrior named Mathilde. In Christian tradition, Mathilda is associated with courage, strength, and faith.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of courage and faith in the face of adversity
data.numerology_meaning: Those with a life path number 9 are natural leaders and teachers. They have the ability to inspire others and to bring about change.

in_hebrew.name: מתילדה
in_hebrew.meaning: מגן של האלוהים, תינוקת קדושה, עזרה, תמיד
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מגן של האלוהים, היא תינוקת קדושה, עזרה, תמיד. שם נשים גרמני שמקורו במיל 'maht' - עזרה, ו-'hild' - ילד. מתילדה היא פרי של שם נשים נפוץ באירופה, ושמן של נוצריים, שסמלם הוא קדושה, תקווה ואור. השם נזכר בפי העם כשם של רופאה, רופא, וגם כשם של כלב, אך גם בשם של קדושה, כפי שמופיע בספר 'האדום' של 'אפולוני'.

in_greek.name: Ματθίλδα
in_greek.meaning: προστασία του Θεού, αγία παιδιά, βοήθεια, αιωνόβια
in_greek.long_meaning: Προστασία του Θεού, η Ματθίλδα είναι αγία παιδιά, βοήθεια, αιωνόβια. Ο όρος Ματθίλδα προέρχεται από τις λέξεις 'μαθ' - βοήθεια και 'hild' - παιδί. Η Ματθίλδα είναι ένα κοινό όνομα γυναικών στην Ευρώπη, που συμβολίζει την αγιαότητα, την ελπίδα και το φως. Στη λαϊκή παράδοση, ο όρος Ματθίλδα συνδέεται με την ονομασία ενός αθλήματος, ενός θεραπευτή, και ακόμη και ενός κτηνού. Ωστόσο, είναι επίσης γνωστό ως όνομα μιας αγίας, όπως φαίνεται στο 'Απάνθισμα' του 'Απολλιναρίου'.

in_latin.name: Mathilda
in_latin.meaning: Dei tutela, sancta pueritia, auxilium, aeterna
in_latin.long_meaning: Dei tutela, Mathilda est sancta pueritia, auxilium, aeterna. Nomen femininum Germanicum, a vocabulis 'maht' - auxilium et 'hild' - pueritia derivatum. Mathilda nomen est commune in Europa, quod symbolum est sanctitatis, spei, et luminis. In populari traditione, nomen Mathilda conexum est cum nomine athletae, medici, et animalis. Tamen, est etiam nomen sanctae, ut apparet in 'Florilegio' Apollinarii.

in_english.name: Mathilda
in_english.meaning: Guardian of God, holy child, help, eternal
in_english.long_meaning: Guardian of God, Mathilda is a holy child, help, eternal. The name Mathilda originates from the words 'maht' - help and 'hild' - child. Mathilda is a common name for women in Europe, symbolizing sanctity, hope, and light. In popular tradition, the name Mathilda is associated with the name of an athlete, a healer, and even an animal. However, it is also known as the name of a saint, as seen in the 'Flower Crown' of Apollinaris. As a name, Mathilda is often associated with qualities such as protection, guidance, and wisdom. In Christian tradition, it is believed that Mathilda holds the power to bring hope and comfort to those who bear it.

saint_reference.note: Saint Matilda of Ringelheim was a queen and nun who lived in the 10th century. She was known for her piety, her charitable works, and her role in the conversion of her husband, Henry the Fowler, to Christianity. She is the patron saint of several cities and regions in Germany and is celebrated for her intercession and her example of Christian living.
